skill.intent: Determine whether a claimed tax amount attributed to a specified progressive-tax subclause follows from the taxpayer's current filing status, taxable income, and the current statutory bracket schedule.

inputs.question: For the current claimed filing-status schedule, what are the lower income bounds of all brackets in order, using zero for the first bracket?

inputs.name: bracket_upper_bounds
inputs.question: For the current claimed filing-status schedule, what are the upper income bounds of all brackets in order, using -1 only for an open-ended final bracket?

inputs.question: What fixed base tax amounts correspond in order to the brackets of the current claimed filing-status schedule, using zero for a bracket with no fixed base?

raw_block.rationale: Targets the airline trigger with the retained position-based reasoning skeleton, while using individually readable checked-position fees and aligned excess-fee bands that were successfully extracted on the closely matched history case.

skill.intent: Compute the exact ticket-plus-bag-fee total by classifying cabin items, assigning checked-bag position fees, and applying the higher applicable overweight or oversize fee to each checked bag.

inputs.name: ticket_price
inputs.question: What is the current passenger's integer ticket price?

inputs.name: lengths
inputs.question: What are the outside lengths in inches of the current passenger's items, in stated order?

inputs.name: widths
inputs.question: What are the outside widths in inches of the current passenger's items, in stated order?

inputs.name: heights
inputs.question: What are the outside heights in inches of the current passenger's items, in stated order?

inputs.name: weights
inputs.question: What are the weights in pounds of the current passenger's items, in stated order?

inputs.name: personal_limits
inputs.question: What ordered length, width, and height limits apply to one personal item under the current source?

inputs.name: carryon_limits
inputs.question: What ordered length, width, and height limits apply to one carry-on bag under the current source?

inputs.name: first_checked_fee
inputs.question: For the current itinerary and cabin, what is the numeric base fee for the first checked bag?

inputs.name: second_checked_fee
inputs.question: For the current itinerary and cabin, what is the numeric base fee for the second checked bag?

inputs.name: third_checked_fee
inputs.question: For the current itinerary and cabin, what is the numeric base fee for the third checked bag?

inputs.name: fourth_plus_checked_fee
inputs.question: For the current itinerary and cabin, what numeric base fee applies to each fourth or later checked bag?

inputs.name: weight_limits_by_checked_position
inputs.question: For each resulting checked-bag position, what standard weight limit applies after accounting for the current cabin and any complimentary status?

inputs.name: overweight_upper_bounds
inputs.question: What ascending weight upper bounds cover the standard and applicable overweight bands for the current route, including the standard band?

inputs.name: overweight_fees
inputs.question: What numeric fees align with the current route's weight bands, including zero for the standard band?

inputs.name: size_upper_bounds
inputs.question: What ascending total-dimension upper bounds cover the standard and applicable oversize bands for the current route, including the standard band?

inputs.name: size_fees
inputs.question: What numeric fees align with the current route's size bands, including zero for the standard band?

outputs.name: answer
outputs.description: The exact current ticket price plus all applicable checked-bag, overweight, and oversize fees.

origin.quote: You're allowed 1 carry-on bag and 1 personal item in all cabins.

source_obligations.statement: Determine each checked bag's size by summing its three outside dimensions.

origin.quote: We calculate the size limits of your bag by adding the total outside dimensions of each bag, length + width + height.

source_obligations.statement: When a checked bag exceeds both weight and size standards, add only the higher excess fee to its checked-position fee.

origin.quote: The higher fee between oversize and overweight applies, in addition to the checked bag fee.

source_provenance.quote: Your personal item like a purse or small handbag must fit under the seat in front of you. Dimensions should not exceed 18 x 14 x 8 inches (45 x 35 x 20 cm).
The total size of your carry-on, including the handles and wheels, cannot exceed 22 x 14 x 9 inches (56 x 36 x 23 cm) and must fit in the sizer at the airport.
More than one fee may apply per bag that exceeds standard dimensions for both weight and size. The higher fee between oversize and overweight applies, in addition to the checked bag fee.

raw_block.rationale: Targets the third trigger with the specific §151(d)(2) dependency: an exemption deduction allowable to another taxpayer makes the individual's own exemption amount zero.

outputs.name: answer
outputs.description: The native binary label: Entailment only when the amount claimed under §151(d)(2) equals the required zero amount, otherwise Contradiction.

raw_block.rationale: Jointly targets all three trigger failures: a focused airline calculator uses separate current-source reads so position fees and excess-fee bands are less likely to be omitted, while an Illinois-specific residual-property planner prevents misclassification under the wearing-apparel provision and emits either EC or EV native output. The airline helper also preserves and can improve the history airline case because it applies the same route, cabin, size, weight, and higher-excess-fee rules.

raw_block.rationale: Create one coupled exemption-pair reader and two schema-specific terminal formatters. The shared reader identifies only directly claimable exemptions under the already-solved applicable law, while the terminal helpers prevent EC citation strings from being confused with EV citation/value records. The generalized applicable-law reading also supports the existing Federal/Wisconsin history parent instead of hard-coding Illinois.
